title.narrative: Microenterprise Development Project

description.narrative: The project aims to promote microenterprise development for inclusive economic growth and poverty reduction. It will support improving microenterprise access to finance through the Palli Karma Sahayak Foundation (PKSF), an apex development finance and capacity building organization; and its partner organizations (POs), which are selected microfinance institutions (MFIs). The overall project comprises (i) a financial intermediary loan of $50 million for a credit line to the PKSF and (ii) a TA grant of $500,000 for building capacity for microenterprise development.

Reports and Recommendations of the President
1.a. As of September 2022, total microenterprise loan outstanding of PKSF to POs has increased to BDT 33.31 billion, of which BDT 4.91 billion is for COVID-19 affected micro entrepreneurs.
1.b. As of September 2022, total microenterprise loan portfolio outstanding of PKSFs POs has increased to BDT 228 billion, of which 80% are for the female borrowers.
1.c. Initiatives have been taken by PKSF to implement the agreed recommendations of the medium-term institutional strengthening and financing strategy.
2.a. Gender-inclusive microenterprise finance operational guidelines are being implemented by MFIs.

2.b. As of September 2022, total 77 officers of 77 POs have been trained on microenterprise lending operations. A batchwise training event has been held for the staff of 120 POs from October to November 2022.

2.c. As of September 2022, 99,224 microenterprise borrowers out of 247,282 of the 6 POs have been enrolled in Mobile Financial Services (MFS) application, who are able to make transactions using their own or family member's MFS account.
3.a. As of September 2022, an enterprise cluster development support scheme for 6 enterprise clusters is being implemented covering 2992 microenterprise borrowers, of whom 71% are female.
3.b. 6 products have been supported for branding. These products have also been uploaded in different e-commerce /f-commerce platform.
As of September 2022, Microenterprise borrowers of PKSF's POs have increased to 2.27 million, of whom 55,593 are affected by COVID-19 and 80% are women borrowers.

Besides, 900 staff from the 6 POs have been trained on MFS system implementation. The trained PO staff have further trained 11,416 microenterprise borrowers on using MFS system, covering 70% are female.
